mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Dobereiner’s triads is a common misconception?

options.A: Elements in a triad have similar chemical properties.
options.B: The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the average of the other two.
options.C: All three elements in a triad have exactly the same atomic mass.
options.D: Dobereiner’s triads were an early attempt to group elements by property.

mcqs.answer: All three elements in a triad have exactly the same atomic mass.
mcqs.explanation: Dobereiner’s triads grouped elements with similar properties and noted that the atomic mass of the middle element is roughly the average of the other two. It is incorrect to think the three elements have identical atomic masses; their masses differ, only the average relationship holds. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the triads, while C is the misconception.

mcqs.question: Newlands observed that every eighth element exhibited similar properties when elements were arranged by increasing atomic mass. Why does this law break down for heavier elements?

options.A: Heavier elements have irregular increments in atomic mass, so the ‘eighth’ spacing no longer aligns with similar properties.
options.B: The discovery of noble gases disrupted the octaves pattern.
options.C: Atomic number, not atomic mass, becomes the governing factor for periodicity in heavier elements.
options.D: Chemical reactivity becomes independent of atomic mass beyond the first 20 elements.

mcqs.answer: Heavier elements have irregular increments in atomic mass, so the ‘eighth’ spacing no longer aligns with similar properties.
mcqs.explanation: Newlands’ octaves worked only because early elements had relatively uniform mass differences. As atomic mass differences grew irregular, the fixed interval of eight no longer corresponded to similar properties, causing the law to fail. Option B is unrelated, C describes the modern periodic law but does not directly explain Newlands’ failure, and D is inaccurate.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares Mendeleev’s periodic law with the modern periodic law?

options.A: Mendeleev arranged elements by increasing atomic number, while the modern law uses atomic mass.
options.B: Mendeleev’s law was based on atomic mass, whereas the modern law is based on atomic number.
options.C: Both laws rely exclusively on the valence electron configuration of elements.
options.D: Mendeleev’s periodic table placed hydrogen above lithium, a placement retained in the modern table.

mcqs.answer: Mendeleev’s law was based on atomic mass, whereas the modern law is based on atomic number.
mcqs.explanation: Mendeleev organized elements by increasing atomic mass and noted periodicity of properties, leaving gaps for undiscovered elements. The modern periodic law, established after Moseley’s work, orders elements by increasing atomic number, which resolves the exceptions in Mendeleev’s table. Option A reverses the criteria, C is false because early laws did not consider electron configuration, and D is incorrect regarding hydrogen’s placement.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise achievements and limitations of Mendeleev classification
mcqs.question: In competitive examinations, which pair correctly describes an achievement and a limitation of Mendeleev’s classification?

options.A: Achievement: Predicted properties of undiscovered elements; Limitation: Could not explain isotopic variations.
options.B: Achievement: Introduced the concept of atomic number; Limitation: Placed elements with similar properties far apart.
options.C: Achievement: Organized elements by increasing atomic mass; Limitation: Failed to predict the existence of noble gases.
options.D: Achievement: Accurately accounted for all atomic mass irregularities; Limitation: Ignored chemical reactivity trends.

mcqs.answer: Achievement: Predicted properties of undiscovered elements; Limitation: Could not explain isotopic variations.
mcqs.explanation: Mendeleev’s table was celebrated for correctly forecasting the existence and properties of elements such as gallium and germanium. However, because it was based on atomic mass, it could not address isotopic differences or the later discovery that atomic number, not mass, is the fundamental ordering principle. Option B incorrectly credits Mendeleev with atomic number, C misstates his prediction of noble gases (which were later added), and D falsely claims he resolved all mass irregularities.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was an early attempt to classify elements before the development of the modern periodic table?

options.D: The modern block classification (s, p, d, f)

mcqs.explanation: Dobereiner’s triads (early 19th century) grouped elements with similar properties in sets of three, representing one of the first systematic classification attempts. Mendeleev’s table, Moseley’s ordering, and the modern block classification came later, after the period discussed in the question.

mcqs.question: What is the defining characteristic of a Dobereiner triad?

options.A: All three elements have identical atomic numbers.
options.B: The atomic mass of the middle element is roughly the average of the other two, and all three share similar chemical properties.
options.C: The three elements belong to the same group in the modern periodic table.
options.D: Each element in the triad has a valence electron configuration ending in s².

mcqs.answer: The atomic mass of the middle element is roughly the average of the other two, and all three share similar chemical properties.
mcqs.explanation: Dobereiner observed that certain groups of three elements (triads) exhibited similar chemical behavior and that the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two. Options A, C, and D describe modern concepts not related to Dobereiner’s original observation.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines Newlands’ law of octaves and distinguishes it from Mendeleev’s periodic law?

options.A: Newlands arranged elements by increasing atomic number and noted that every eighth element showed similar properties; Mendeleev used atomic mass.
options.B: Newlands grouped elements in sets of eight based on similar properties when ordered by atomic mass; Mendeleev’s law was based on atomic mass but did not use a fixed interval.
options.C: Newlands’ law was based on electron configuration, whereas Mendeleev’s law relied on valence shells.
options.D: Both Newlands and Mendeleev used the same criteria, but Newlands published his work a decade earlier.

mcqs.answer: Newlands grouped elements in sets of eight based on similar properties when ordered by atomic mass; Mendeleev’s law was based on atomic mass but did not use a fixed interval.
mcqs.explanation: Newlands observed that when elements were listed by increasing atomic mass, every eighth element exhibited similar properties, coining the “law of octaves.” Mendeleev also used atomic mass for ordering but arranged elements to reflect periodicity without imposing a strict eight‑element interval. Option A incorrectly mentions atomic number for Newlands, C confuses with modern electronic theory, and D incorrectly states they used identical criteria.

mcqs.question: According to Mendeleev’s periodic law, which of the following predictions is most justified?

options.A: An element with atomic mass 65 will exhibit properties similar to those of chlorine.
options.B: An undiscovered element placed between silicon (atomic mass 28) and phosphorus (atomic mass 31) should have properties intermediate between them.
options.C: All elements with atomic masses greater than 200 will be metals.
options.D: Elements in the same period will always have the same atomic mass.

mcqs.answer: An undiscovered element placed between silicon (atomic mass 28) and phosphorus (atomic mass 31) should have properties intermediate between them.
mcqs.explanation: Mendeleev’s law allowed him to predict the existence and properties of elements that fit into gaps in his table. Placing an unknown element between Si and P (both in the same group) would imply it shares intermediate chemical characteristics. Option A is incorrect because chlorine’s properties are not determined solely by atomic mass, C is an overgeneralization, and D is false because atomic mass varies within a period.
